verdict.rationale: Ramp documents its own rules-based approval workflows that route requests to the right stakeholders by vendor type, spend category, or dollar amount. These approval workflows apply across cards, reimbursements, bills, and agent purchases. However, nothing in the evidence shows explicit sequential multi-step chains (manager → budget owner → finance), approver delegation, or time-based escalation when approvers sit on requests. The AI agent's "escalates when it's not [safe]" is risk-flagging, not stale-approval escalation, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: explicit multi-step sequential chain configuration with named roles (manager, budget owner, finance), approver delegation/out-of-office reassignment, SLA-based escalation or reminders for pending approvals, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can build multi-step approval chains — manager, budget owner, finance — with delegation and escalation when approvers sit on requests

citations.quote: Rules-based workflows route requests to the right stakeholders automatically based on vendor type, spend category, or dollar amount
Create personalized workflows that only notify the right people, based on spend amount or team role, and keep visibility high.
budgets, templates, and approval workflows that apply equally to cards, reimbursements, bills, and agent purchases
